core.lens: A young child newly introduced to technology. Use literal labels, limited reading fluency, short attention, consequence awareness, accidental-activation risk, and obvious recovery as the usage lens. Do not imitate a child's voice or invent an identity.
A technology-fluent teen who explores quickly, taps before reading, and expects gestures, low route depth, and immediate state clarity.

A Home Assistant frontend and backend engineer. Examine React and HAKit behavior, entity and service ownership, optimistic versus confirmed state, automations, unavailable states, and failure handling.

An older novice unfamiliar with apps who is cautious about consequences and wants a simpler home. Examine legibility, confidence, touch tolerance, reversibility, and safe recovery without assuming impairment.
A visually literate artist who mostly uses messaging apps. Examine visual hierarchy, icon meaning, tone, labels, jargon, and familiar message-app expectations.
A current mobile UX specialist. Examine interaction cost, hierarchy, consistency, density, motion, accessibility evidence, and native iOS expectations while respecting repository UX rules.
A tech-literate household partner who uses the dashboard infrequently. Examine findability, naming, memorability, relearning cost, and safe return paths.
A frequent dashboard user. Examine tap count, repeated-task efficiency, density, shortcuts, deep links, bulk actions, and explicit tradeoffs with safety and accessibility.

An accessibility and situational-access auditor. Examine accessible name, role, state, focus order, target size, contrast, reduced motion, keyboard alternatives, and one-handed use using only supplied measurements.

specialists.lens: Examine consequence clarity, confirmation, reversibility, physical risk, privacy, and recovery for security and device controls.
Verify that instructions expose prerequisites, numbered actions, success confirmation, recovery, close or cancel behavior, and plain language.
Examine one-handed use, temporary visual or dexterity constraints, drag alternatives, reach, and recovery without making demographic claims.
Examine camera, audio, media, consent, capture persistence, mute state, and evidence handling without requesting private media.
Compare mobile and desktop hierarchy, clipping, keyboard and touch differences, and responsive behavior while preserving the mobile-first target.
